S41.what: Takes deposits and lends to Singapore SMEs and consumers - a licensed finance company, not a full bank.
S41.rev: Net interest income from SME loans, property loans and hire purchase, funded by fixed deposits. Singapore only.
S41.gm: Watch net interest margin, the loan book size, non-performing loans and the very high capital ratio - it is deliberately overcapitalised.
S41.mgmt: Part of the Hong Leong Group (Kwek family). Managed conservatively, with a large equity base relative to the loan book.
S41.comp: DBS, OCBC and UOB in SME lending; other finance companies; private credit funds.
S41.moat: A finance company licence and long SME relationships, but it competes with banks that have cheaper funding.
S41.ind: Singapore SME credit demand is steady; margins compress when rates fall.
S41.risk: Falling interest rates compressing the deposit-to-loan spread that drives nearly all earnings.
S41.implied: Trading below book value with a high dividend implies low growth and rate-driven earnings decline.
S41.debate: Bulls say a heavily overcapitalised lender below book with a solid dividend. Bears note structurally low returns on equity and no growth.
S41.disprove: Net interest margin compressing; loan book shrinking; non-performing loans rising; dividend cut.

Q5T.what: Owns Singapore hotels and serviced residences - Village, Quincy, Oasia and Rendezvous brands - and leases them to Far East Hospitality operators.
Q5T.rev: Hotel and serviced residence master leases in Singapore, with income linked to RevPAR performance through variable rent.
Q5T.gm: REIT metrics: gearing in the low 30s, occupancy tracking Singapore tourism, and the master lease structure providing a fixed rent floor.
Q5T.mgmt: Sponsored by Far East Organization (the Ng family) with Woh Hup and other partners.
Q5T.comp: CDL Hospitality Trusts and other Singapore hospitality owners.
Q5T.moat: Singapore hotel real estate near MRT and business districts - scarcity of hotel sites is the underlying support.
Q5T.ind: Singapore tourism has recovered; room rates surged in 2023-24 and have since normalised.
Q5T.risk: Room rates normalising further from an unusually strong period, reducing variable rent.
Q5T.implied: A high yield implies flat-to-declining RevPAR expectations.
Q5T.debate: Bulls say Singapore tourism growth plus a fixed rent floor and low gearing. Bears note rates have peaked and the portfolio is small.
Q5T.disprove: RevPAR declining year over year; occupancy falling; distribution per unit declining; gearing rising.

AU8U.what: Owns shopping malls, business parks and logistics properties in Chinese cities and collects rent in renminbi.
AU8U.rev: Retail malls are the majority of income, with business parks and logistics the rest. Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu and other tier one and two cities.
AU8U.gm: REIT metrics: gearing around 40-42%, occupancy in the 90s, with renminbi income translated into Singapore dollars.
AU8U.mgmt: Managed by CapitaLand Investment as sponsor, with a China-specific mandate.
AU8U.comp: Other China-focused property owners; domestic Chinese REITs are now emerging.
AU8U.moat: Established mall locations in Chinese cities managed by CapitaLand - operating capability rather than irreplaceable assets.
AU8U.ind: Chinese retail consumption has been weak; business park demand is soft with oversupply.
AU8U.risk: Chinese property values continuing to fall, forcing valuation write-downs and pressuring gearing.
AU8U.implied: A very high yield and a deep discount to book imply the market expects further Chinese weakness.
AU8U.debate: Bulls say deeply discounted Chinese assets with any recovery providing upside. Bears say Chinese commercial property is a value trap with currency risk on top.
AU8U.disprove: Tenant sales declining; occupancy falling; further valuation write-downs; gearing above 43%; distribution cut.

EH5.what: Develops residential and commercial property in Malaysia and Australia - apartments in Kuala Lumpur and Melbourne.
EH5.rev: Property development in Malaysia (the majority) and Australia, plus investment properties and hospitality.
EH5.gm: Development margins are reasonable; the company is conservatively financed but has very thin trading liquidity on SGX.
EH5.mgmt: Controlled by the Kong family, who are also behind United Overseas Australia's Malaysian operations.
EH5.comp: Malaysian developers - Sunway, SP Setia, IOI Properties - and Melbourne apartment developers.
EH5.moat: Land bank in Kuala Lumpur at low historical cost. Not a competitive moat.
EH5.ind: Malaysian property demand is moderate; Australian apartment demand is constrained by construction costs.
EH5.risk: Malaysian ringgit weakness and property oversupply in Kuala Lumpur.
EH5.implied: Trading far below book value implies the market heavily discounts Malaysian development assets.
EH5.debate: Bulls point at a persistent, very deep discount to net asset value. Bears note minimal liquidity, family control and a discount that has never closed.
EH5.disprove: Development sales slowing; net asset value declining; no buybacks or dividends; liquidity worsening.

Z25.what: Develops high-end residential property in Chinese tier one and two cities, plus Singapore projects.
Z25.rev: Chinese residential development (Shanghai, Nanjing, Suzhou, Shenzhen) is the bulk, with Singapore and investment properties the rest.
Z25.gm: Development gross margins have compressed sharply as Chinese property prices fell; cash collection and debt maturity profile matter more than margin now.
Z25.mgmt: Founder Zhong Sheng Jian controls the company. It has been one of the more conservatively financed Chinese developers.
Z25.comp: China Vanke, China Resources Land, Longfor and other Chinese developers - many of which have defaulted.
Z25.moat: A reputation for build quality in the premium Chinese segment and land in good locations - but the sector's problems overwhelm company-specific strengths.
Z25.ind: Chinese residential property is in a multi-year contraction with weak sales and falling prices.
Z25.risk: Chinese property prices falling further, impairing inventory and squeezing the ability to refinance.
Z25.implied: Trading at a fraction of book value implies the market expects substantial further write-downs.
Z25.debate: Bulls say it survived the sector purge with better finances than most and trades at a deep discount. Bears say Chinese property has no visible bottom.
Z25.disprove: Contracted sales declining; inventory impairments; net gearing rising; bond maturities not refinanced.

J85.what: Owns hotels in Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, the UK, Germany, Italy, Japan and the Maldives, and a Singapore retail mall.
J85.rev: Singapore hotels are the largest contributor, with the overseas portfolio providing diversification and volatility.
J85.gm: REIT metrics: gearing around 40%, RevPAR by market, and a master lease structure on the Singapore hotels providing a rent floor.
J85.mgmt: Sponsored by City Developments (the Kwek family), which also holds a large stake.
J85.comp: Far East Hospitality Trust in Singapore; global hotel owners in each overseas market.
J85.moat: Singapore hotel real estate with limited new supply; the overseas assets are more ordinary.
J85.ind: Singapore hotel rates normalised after a 2023-24 peak; European and Japanese assets have improved.
J85.risk: Singapore RevPAR declining while gearing is already at 40%, squeezing distributions.
J85.implied: A high yield and a large discount to book imply the market expects flat to falling distributions.
J85.debate: Bulls say hotel assets at a deep discount with tourism recovery upside. Bears note gearing, a scattered portfolio and years of distribution decline.
J85.disprove: Singapore RevPAR falling; overseas assets underperforming; gearing above 42%; distribution cut.

T6I.what: Runs pawnbroking shops, moneylending and retail of gold and jewellery in Singapore and Malaysia.
T6I.rev: Pawnbroking interest income, retail and trading of jewellery and gold, and secured moneylending. Singapore is the largest market.
T6I.gm: Pawnbroking earns high interest spreads on gold-collateralised loans; gold retail carries thinner margins but rising gold prices lift both.
T6I.mgmt: The Yeah family founded and controls the business. Conservative expansion and consistent dividends.
T6I.moat: Licensed pawnbroking with collateral-backed lending - regulated entry and a physical shop network in dense locations.
T6I.ind: Pawnbroking demand rises when credit is tight; high gold prices increase loan values and retail margins.
T6I.risk: A sharp fall in gold prices reducing both collateral values and jewellery retail profits.
T6I.implied: A low-teens P/E implies continued gold-driven earnings growth rather than a cyclical peak.
T6I.debate: Bulls say a well-run, cash-generative lender benefiting directly from high gold prices. Bears note earnings are levered to a single commodity.
T6I.disprove: Gold prices falling sharply; pledge book shrinking; retail margins compressing; default rates rising.

RE4.what: Mines and trades Indonesian thermal coal, mainly low-calorific coal sold to China and India.
RE4.rev: Coal mining and coal trading from Indonesian concessions, with a new mine (TRA) being developed to extend reserve life.
RE4.gm: Margins track the coal price against cash cost per tonne. Geo Energy is a low-cost producer but has limited reserve life without new mines.
RE4.mgmt: Charles Antonny Melati and the founding group control it. Capital allocation has included buybacks and dividends.
RE4.comp: Other Indonesian coal miners - Adaro, Bumi Resources, Bayan.
RE4.moat: Low cash cost per tonne and concession ownership - a commodity cost position, nothing more.
RE4.ind: Thermal coal demand in Asia has been more resilient than expected, but the long-term direction is down.
RE4.risk: Coal prices falling, or the new mine and infrastructure (hauling road, jetty) being delayed or over budget.
RE4.implied: A very low P/E implies the market expects coal prices and earnings to decline - a terminal value discount.
RE4.debate: Bulls say cheap cash flows, net cash and a high dividend from a low-cost producer. Bears say thermal coal is a declining industry and the reserve life is short.
RE4.disprove: Coal prices falling below cash cost; new mine development delayed; production guidance missed; dividend cut.

F9D.what: Provides energy engineering, industrial real estate development, geospatial software (Esri distribution) and healthcare technology in Asia Pacific.
F9D.rev: Real estate solutions, energy engineering and geospatial technology are the three pillars; geospatial is the highest-margin recurring business.
F9D.gm: Geospatial (Esri licence distribution in Australia) carries software-like margins; engineering is project-based and lumpier.
F9D.mgmt: Wong Fong Fui has led it for decades and holds a large stake. Boustead Projects, the real estate arm, was partly separated.
F9D.comp: Esri competitors in geospatial; regional engineering firms in energy; industrial developers in real estate.
F9D.moat: Exclusive Esri distribution rights in Australia is a genuinely valuable franchise; the rest is project engineering.
F9D.ind: Geospatial demand from government and utilities is growing; energy engineering follows oil and gas capex.
F9D.risk: Losing the Esri distribution agreement, which would remove the most valuable recurring earnings stream.
F9D.implied: A low P/E with a large net cash position implies little growth is expected.
F9D.debate: Bulls say net cash is a large share of the market cap and the geospatial business is undervalued. Bears note lumpy engineering earnings and a persistent conglomerate discount.
F9D.disprove: Esri agreement terms changing; engineering order book shrinking; net cash being spent poorly; dividend cut.

544.what: Provides industrial automation, communications and electrification solutions to energy, infrastructure and mining customers, mainly in the US, Australia and Asia.
544.rev: The Americas (largely US electrification and infrastructure) is the largest market, Asia Pacific and EMEA the rest. Order intake is the key metric.
544.gm: Gross margin in the high 20s to low 30s. Project execution risk is the main threat to margins.
544.mgmt: Lim Boon Kheng is CEO; Heliconia (a Temasek unit) has been a substantial shareholder.
544.comp: Larger automation and engineering firms - Honeywell, Yokogawa - and regional electrical contractors.
544.moat: Customer relationships and technical certifications in niche industrial systems; modest switching costs.
544.ind: US electrification and data centre infrastructure spending has driven strong order growth.
544.risk: Project cost overruns, which have hurt earnings before, or a slowdown in US infrastructure spending.
544.implied: A mid-teens P/E implies the order book converts at current margins.
544.debate: Bulls point at a record order book from US electrification with a decent dividend. Bears remember past project write-downs and note thin margins.
544.disprove: Order intake declining; project provisions; margins compressing; receivables rising faster than revenue.

P9D.what: Builds and fabricates heavy engineering structures and provides maintenance services to Australian resources, energy and defence projects.
P9D.rev: Australian resources and energy construction and maintenance, plus a growing defence shipbuilding and infrastructure segment.
P9D.gm: Construction margins are thin; the maintenance contracts provide steadier, better-quality earnings.
P9D.mgmt: Patrick Tallon is CEO; the founding management holds shares. Dual-listed in Singapore and Australia.
P9D.comp: Monadelphous, Lycopodium and other Australian engineering contractors.
P9D.moat: Purpose-built heavy fabrication facilities in Western Australia and defence security clearances - genuine but narrow.
P9D.ind: Australian resources maintenance spending is steady; defence infrastructure is growing.
P9D.risk: Project losses or a downturn in Australian mining capex, which drives most of the revenue.
P9D.implied: A low-teens P/E implies continued order book conversion at current margins.
P9D.debate: Bulls like the defence diversification and a strong order book. Bears note construction is a thin-margin business with execution risk.
P9D.disprove: Order book declining; project provisions; Australian mining capex cuts; margin compression.

S20.what: A holding company with tin smelting (Malaysia Smelting), property investment in Singapore and Malaysia, and hospitality assets.
S20.rev: Resources (tin smelting and mining through Malaysia Smelting Corporation), real estate (including a stake in ARA-linked assets) and hospitality.
S20.gm: Look through to the listed stakes: Malaysia Smelting Corporation is separately listed, so much of the value is observable.
S20.mgmt: Chew Gek Khim is executive chairman; the Tan Chin Tuan family controls it. Long-term, conservative stewardship.
S20.comp: Other tin producers (Yunnan Tin) and, for the property arm, Singapore real estate companies.
S20.moat: One of the world's few large independent tin smelters - a genuinely scarce asset - plus long-held property.
S20.ind: Tin demand is tied to electronics soldering and has a tight supply picture; prices have been strong.
S20.risk: Tin price declines and the holding company discount persisting.
S20.implied: A deep discount to the sum of its parts implies the market applies a permanent conglomerate penalty.
S20.debate: Bulls say a discounted basket including a strategically scarce tin smelter. Bears note illiquidity, complexity and a structural discount.
S20.disprove: Tin prices falling; Malaysia Smelting earnings declining; property values falling; the discount widening.

5WJ.what: Operates pawnbroking outlets, secured lending and retail of gold, jewellery and luxury watches in Singapore and Malaysia.
5WJ.rev: Retail and trading of gold and luxury items is the largest revenue line; pawnbroking interest income carries the higher margin.
5WJ.gm: Pawnbroking spreads are high; luxury retail margins are thinner but volumes are larger. Gold prices drive both.
5WJ.mgmt: Founder Lim Yong Guan and family control the business. Expansion has been steady across both markets.
5WJ.comp: ValueMax, Maxi-Cash (Aspial), and licensed moneylenders and luxury watch retailers.
5WJ.moat: Licensed pawnbroking with regulated entry, a shop network and a growing pre-owned luxury watch business.
5WJ.ind: High gold prices have lifted both the pledge book and retail margins across the sector.
5WJ.risk: A sharp gold price fall, or luxury watch inventory losing value in a weak secondary market.
5WJ.implied: A low-teens P/E implies continued growth from gold-linked earnings.
5WJ.debate: Bulls say a growing, cash-generative lender with gold price leverage. Bears note inventory risk in luxury watches and dependence on one commodity.
5WJ.disprove: Gold prices falling; pledge book shrinking; luxury watch inventory write-downs; margin compression.

5UF.what: Retails jewellery and branded merchandise and runs the Maxi-Cash pawnbroking and secured lending chain in Singapore.
5UF.rev: Retail and trading of jewellery and branded merchandise is the largest line; pawnbroking and secured lending the higher-margin part.
5UF.gm: Similar economics to peers: pawnbroking spreads are wide, jewellery retail thinner. Gold prices drive the results.
5UF.mgmt: Part of the Aspial group controlled by the Koh family, following a restructuring that separated the property business.
5UF.comp: ValueMax and MoneyMax in pawnbroking; jewellery retailers in Singapore.
5UF.moat: Licensed pawnbroking and a retail network, plus the Maxi-Cash brand - similar to peers, with no particular edge.
5UF.ind: Gold-linked earnings have been strong across the Singapore pawnbroking sector.
5UF.risk: Gold price reversal and the group's history of related-party complexity and leverage.
5UF.implied: The valuation implies continued gold-driven earnings with the restructuring behind it.
5UF.debate: Bulls say gold price leverage at a modest multiple after simplification. Bears note the group's leverage history and weaker positioning than ValueMax or MoneyMax.
5UF.disprove: Gold prices falling; pledge book shrinking; debt rising; related-party transactions increasing.

H30.what: Owns and manages Singapore commercial and residential property - International Building and Concorde Hotel on Orchard Road.
H30.rev: Rental income from Singapore investment properties plus hotel operations. A small, closely held property company.
H30.gm: Look at rental income, the valuation of the Orchard Road assets and the very large discount to net asset value.
H30.mgmt: The Cheong family controls it and has been criticised by minority shareholders for the persistent discount and low payout.
H30.comp: Other Singapore property owners; for shareholders, any Singapore REIT offers the same exposure with better liquidity.
H30.moat: Orchard Road property ownership - scarce real estate, but no operating advantage.
H30.ind: Singapore commercial property is stable; Orchard Road retail has recovered with tourism.
H30.risk: The discount never closing; management has shown little urgency about unlocking value.
H30.implied: Trading at a fraction of book value implies the market expects no monetisation.
H30.debate: Bulls say prime Orchard Road assets at a deep discount. Bears note minimal liquidity, a low dividend and family control with no catalyst.
H30.disprove: Net asset value per share declining; rental income falling; no capital return; the discount widening.

LJ3.what: Develops and invests in property in Singapore and manages hospitality and healthcare assets, and sponsors OUE REIT.
LJ3.rev: Real estate (investment properties and fund management), healthcare (Indonesian and Chinese hospitals), and other segments.
LJ3.gm: Watch recurring rental income, net gearing, and the discount to net asset value. Fund management fees from OUE REIT are a smaller stream.
LJ3.mgmt: Controlled by the Riady-linked Lippo interests. Related-party transactions are a recurring consideration.
LJ3.comp: Singapore property developers and REIT sponsors.
LJ3.moat: Ownership of prime Singapore assets and a REIT management platform - moderate.
LJ3.ind: Singapore commercial property is stable; the healthcare arm is exposed to Indonesia and China.
LJ3.risk: Related-party transactions and a governance discount that has persisted for years.
LJ3.implied: A very deep discount to book implies the market discounts both assets and governance heavily.
LJ3.debate: Bulls say assets worth several times the market cap. Bears cite governance, related-party history and no catalyst.
LJ3.disprove: Net asset value declining; related-party transactions increasing; healthcare losses; the discount widening.

S08.what: Delivers letters and parcels in Singapore, runs the post office network and owns SingPost Centre - in the middle of a major restructuring.
S08.rev: Post and parcel in Singapore plus property rental, following the sale of the Australian logistics business. The domestic postal business is loss-making.
S08.gm: Domestic postal margins are negative without regulatory relief; the property segment (SingPost Centre) is the reliable earner.
S08.mgmt: Leadership changed after the 2024 governance episode and the Australia divestment. Singtel and Alibaba are substantial shareholders.
S08.comp: Ninja Van, J&T Express and other parcel carriers in Singapore; global logistics firms.
S08.moat: The public postal licence and the post office network - a regulated obligation as much as an advantage, given letter volumes are collapsing.
S08.ind: Letter volumes decline every year; e-commerce parcels are competitive and low-margin.
S08.risk: The domestic postal business continuing to lose money with no clear path to profitability after the asset sales are done.
S08.implied: The price reflects the special dividend and asset sales more than operating earnings.
S08.debate: Bulls say post-divestment the company is cash-rich with a valuable property asset. Bears say the remaining core business is structurally loss-making.
S08.disprove: Domestic postal losses continuing; no regulatory relief on postal rates; cash being spent rather than returned; property income falling.

H07.what: Owns and operates Stamford hotels in Australia, plus property development in Australia and Singapore.
H07.rev: Hotel ownership and management in Australia (Sydney, Melbourne, Adelaide, Brisbane, Auckland) plus property development.
H07.gm: Hotel operating margins in Australia plus development profits. The underlying real estate value exceeds the market capitalisation.
H07.mgmt: The Ow family controls it. Very conservative, with net cash and a history of special dividends after asset sales.
H07.comp: Australian hotel owners and Singapore property companies.
H07.moat: Freehold hotel real estate in Australian city centres - asset value rather than competitive advantage.
H07.ind: Australian hotel demand has recovered; development margins depend on the Australian residential market.
H07.risk: Australian property values falling and the persistent discount to net asset value never closing.
H07.implied: Trading at a fraction of net asset value implies the market expects no monetisation.
H07.debate: Bulls say deeply discounted Australian hotel real estate with net cash and occasional special dividends. Bears note thin liquidity and a family that has been in no hurry.
H07.disprove: Australian hotel RevPAR declining; net asset value falling; no asset sales or capital return; development losses.

YF8.what: Manages investments - debt investments, funds, venture capital and wealth management - in China and Singapore, spun off from Yangzijiang Shipbuilding.
YF8.rev: Investment income from a debt investment portfolio in China (transitioning toward Singapore-managed funds), plus fund management fees.
YF8.gm: Look at net asset value per share, the return on the investment portfolio, provisions on Chinese debt investments, and the discount to book.
YF8.mgmt: Spun out of the Yangzijiang group; the Ren family retains influence. The strategy is shifting capital from China debt to Singapore-based funds.
YF8.comp: Other investment managers and holding companies; for shareholders, the discount to book is the point.
YF8.moat: None in the conventional sense - this is a pool of capital being redeployed.
YF8.ind: Chinese private credit has had elevated default rates; the shift to Singapore-managed capital is a de-risking.
YF8.risk: Further provisions on the Chinese debt investment portfolio eroding book value.
YF8.implied: Trading at a large discount to book implies the market expects more write-downs on the China book.
YF8.debate: Bulls say buybacks and a shrinking China exposure should narrow a discount of more than half of book. Bears say the underlying assets are opaque and impairments keep coming.
YF8.disprove: Further impairments on Chinese debt investments; net asset value per share declining; buybacks stopping; fund launches failing to raise capital.

A31.what: Develops satellite communication terminals - including inter-satellite data relay technology for low-earth-orbit satellites - sold to maritime, aviation and space customers.
A31.rev: Satellite terminal products and licensing, with very small absolute revenue relative to the market capitalisation.
A31.gm: Gross margins vary with product mix; the company has been loss-making or marginally profitable for extended periods.
A31.mgmt: Tan Khai Pang is CEO. The founding management retains influence. Repeated capital raisings have diluted shareholders.
A31.comp: Inmarsat/Viasat, Iridium and other satellite terminal manufacturers; a very small player against global incumbents.
A31.moat: Specific patents on inter-satellite data relay technology - genuinely novel, but unproven commercially at scale.
A31.ind: Low-earth-orbit satellite deployment is growing rapidly, which is the thesis for this technology.
A31.risk: Running out of cash before the technology is commercialised - it has needed repeated funding rounds.
A31.implied: The market capitalisation relative to minimal revenue implies investors are pricing a technology option, not a business.
A31.debate: Bulls see a niche technology with real patents in a growing space market. Bears see years of losses, dilution and a valuation disconnected from revenue.
A31.disprove: Revenue not scaling; further equity placements; cash burn continuing; contracts announced but not converting to revenue.
